android.desc:
Andronix runs a full Linux system right inside the app, on your Android phone or tablet. Pick a distro and a desktop, and Andronix does the rest. No root needed ⚡️

LINUX IN THE APP
• One tap installs Linux: ready-made images make it fast.
• Real desktops with sound and optional GPU acceleration (experimental).
• Keyboard and mouse support, and layouts for tablets and foldables.
• Pin Linux apps to your home screen, and share files through Download/Andronix.
• A notification shows what's running and how much memory it uses, with Open and Stop.
• If something fails, Andronix can send a problem report for you (it asks first), and shows the fix right away when it's a known problem.
• In 8 languages, including Russian.

HOW IT WORKS
Andronix runs Linux with PRoot, so nothing on your phone is changed and no root is needed.

LINUX DISTROS, NO ADS
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Debian 13, Kali, Fedora, Arch, Manjaro, Alpine and Void, with your choice of desktop: XFCE, LXQt, MATE or KDE Plasma (KDE on Ubuntu, Debian and Kali). Or the command line only. All free, no ads.

MODDED OS 2.0
Ready-made desktops, styled and tuned by Andronix: Ubuntu XFCE, Ubuntu KDE, Debian XFCE, Manjaro XFCE and Kali XFCE. Buy one edition, or get the Modded Pass for all five, with updates included. If you bought a Classic Modded OS before, it stays yours to install.

ANDRONIX PREMIUM
Early access to new editions and beta installers, higher download limits, a spot on the supporter wall, and a lower price on the Modded Pass. It's also the best way to support Andronix.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
Browse, code, learn Linux, run servers and tools: anything that doesn't need the full Linux kernel. Some things are limited by Android itself (for example, most pen-testing tools that need raw network access).

REQUIREMENTS
• Android 8.0 or newer on a 64-bit ARM (arm64) phone or tablet.
• On phones with a Linux kernel older than 4.8, the app offers LXQt and the command line.
• Older or non-arm64 phones (Android 7.0+), or prefer a command-line installer? Andronix also works through Termux; the app links you to it.

OPEN SOURCE
The Andronix installer and all the free distros are open source on GitHub. The app and Modded OS are how we keep the project going.

HELP AND COMMUNITY
Docs: https://docs.andronix.app
Website: https://andronix.app
Discord: https://chat.andronix.app

quotes.text:
I used to run a full Debian chroot on Android. It was very handy except that if you ran it on an unrooted Android device you couldn't be a user with full root capabilities. But gcc, make, tar, gzip, and git worked well enough to compile working stacks for other languages (the first software I built on it was Perl from source) as a regular user. Thousands of packages available and the ability to build from source, right on my phone in my pocket. They had other distros for it, too. Unfortunately that project - GNURoot - seems abandoned. Possibly fortunately a new one is from the same maintainers. I think I never used X on it.  https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=tech.ula&hl=en_US&gl=US

There's another called Debian noroot (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cuntubuntu&hl=en_US&gl=US) that appears fairly up to date but I haven't tried it. It's well rated but said to be slow. It includes XFCE and apparently starts it by default. It uses PRoot.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=studio.com.techriz.andronix&hl=en_US&gl=US is yet another, and also uses PRoot. I have concerns about their page saying they have closed-source modded versions of F/OSS operating system distros though, and that they'll only provide source to developers who register with them. That's kind of unneighborly if they're customizing BSD or Apache licensed portions of a distro and illegal if they're doing it with GPL or LGPL portions.
